block_set.title: The Scheduling Problem in High-Level Synthesis: Extended 0/1 LP Model and Solution Methods
block_set.sub_firstblock: Hans Achatz Universität Passau Lehrstuhl Rechnerstrukturen (Prof. W. Grass) D-94030 Passau, Germany

block_set.title: 1. INTRODUCTION
block_set.sub_firstblock: High-level synthesis tools transform a behavioral description in terms of algorithm into a RT-level structural description observing several constraints. In order to produce the data path part of a digital processor the following subtasks have to be solved: scheduling, resource allocation and resource binding. This paper is concerned with the scheduling problem as a first step in the sequence of subtasks. Scheduling is the task of assigning operations to control steps optimizing a certain objective function. Several different methods for scheduling have been published. Most of them are heuristics.

block_set.title: 2. 0/1 LP MODEL AND EXTENSIONS
block_set.sub_firstblock: We start with the notation of the 0/1 LP formulations introduced by Lee (1989). A short summary of the abbreviations should make this paper more readable. As soon as possible (ASAP) and as last as possible (ALAP) times are computed for every operation. For simplicity the 0/1 LP model in this introduction is restricted to operations with one cycle propagation delay and function units with only one operation type executable.

block_set.title: 3. GENERATING LOWER BOUNDS VIA LP
block_set.sub_firstblock: The efficiency of solving the $0 / 1 \bf { L P }$ is extremely dependent on good bounds. In our approach we generate lower bounds via LP. In all applications so far we did not have problems with computing times. For determination of these lower bounds we have to distinguish between time-constrained and resource-constrained scheduling. In the time-constrained model we assume that the number of csteps is given and that we want to minimize the hardware costs. If we know how many units of one type are needed at least the solution space would be reduced.
